title.narrative: NIHR DA 1: Intervention to strengthen low-and middle-income country primary care: proposal development for a cross-country comparison

description.narrative:
A low- and middle-income country (LMIC) award led by the Knowledge Translation Unit (KTU) of the University of Cape Town, South Africa, which aims to develop a research collaboration with key government, academic and community stakeholders and a proposal to conduct a comparative study evaluating the implementation of a primary care health system strengthening programme in South Africa, Brazil, Indonesia and Ethiopia.
The programme is called PACK, the Practical Approach to Care Kit. PACK is a system-strengthening programme that comprises a comprehensive clinical decision support tool for primary care and an implementation strategy that addresses health system barriers to its uptake. It has been introduced to all four countries to support primary care reforms and has shown some success in improving health outcomes and quality of care. However, there is limited evidence around how best to localise and implement the programme.
Due to commence in January 2025, the one-year award intends to evaluate how best to ensure that patient care is relevant to local diseases, health worker skills and available resources via the implementation of PACK within health systems in South Africa, Brazil, Indonesia and Ethiopia. While the award focuses on the development of a proposal centred on a cross-country comparative study of PACK implementation, activities also aim to foster research collaboration between KTU and key government, academic and community stakeholders. Increased collaboration between KTU and implementing partners works to bolster research skills, capacity and literacy, as well as efforts to ensure the most appropriate approach to measure successes and challenges of the programme are established.

The award has five objectives:
1. To convene a group focused on the cultivation of a research collaboration between implementing partners across four countries. 2. To identify and address the research collaboration’s capacity-strengthening needs. 3. To determine the research methodology required to conduct a cross-country comparison of the Practical Approach to Care Kit (PACK) implementation experiences. 4. To create a Community Engagement and Involvement methodology. 5. To generate a research proposal focused on the evaluation of cross-country PACK implementation experiences.
